children: Asian equities opened mostly higher on Wednesday, November 18, as a strong Nvidia forecast lifted sentiment after two punishing sessions on Wall Street.

South Korea's Kospi surged 3.08%, the region's biggest mover, while Taiwan's Taiex climbed 1.13% and Japan's Nikkei 225 added 1.03%. The broader Topix slipped 0.20% and Hang Seng futures pointed 0.3% lower.

In India, GIFT Nifty signalled a weaker start despite the Nvidia-led rebound. The Nifty hit a nine-month high of 25,387 on Tuesday recovering all the loses it had incurred since the onset of the US-Iran war on February, up 96 points, while the Sensex gained 427 points to 82,532.
The Nifty Bank index closed 697 points higher at a record 62,273. Foreign institutional investors bought more than $9.5 billion of Indian equities in November, their biggest monthly inflow.
In currencies, the Japanese yen weakened 0.1% to 159.55 per dollar, and the offshore yuan barely moved at 6.6666.

The buying followed a sharp rebound in US equity futures as Nasdaq 100 contracts jumped 1.5% and S&P 500 contracts gained 0.8% in early Asian trade. Dow futures rose 165 points, S&P 500 futures 60 points, and Nasdaq futures nearly 400 points.

The rebound also followed a bruising Tuesday session after the Dow fell 850 points following Monday's 750-point loss, a two-day drop of 1,700 points. The S&P 500 lost 1% and closed at its lowest since July, while the Nasdaq ended 0.7% lower after touching its weakest level since April.

Nvidia drove the move as the chipmaker's shares rose as much as 6% in extended trading on Tuesday after it reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and well above the $109.3 billion analysts expected. Earnings per share (EPS) came in at $2.68 against a forecast of $2.47. Data-centre revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion.

The company's Chairman Harvey Jones said the board will not reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang after he was ousted last week. Interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also chief financial officer, told investors, "It is business as usual at Nvidia."
For the fourth quarter, Nvidia guided to $130 billion, give or take 3%, against the $125.3 billion analysts expected. It also lifted its fiscal 2028 growth forecast to 75% from 70%.

Additionally, markets also seemed to take into account that Anthropic is preparing for what could become the largest artificial intelligence IPO, reflecting strong investor interest in generative AI and the companies developing the technology.
The company is expected to price its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday and begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.
Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, making the listing a closely watched event for investors.

Oil prices steadied in early Asian trade on Wednesday, as traders seemed to weigh renewed fighting in West Asia against signs of recovering supplies. Brent crude traded at $93.49 a barrel, while the US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for December delivery rose 0.3% to settle at $86.01 a barrel in New York.

Fresh flare-ups in the Gulf region drove the latest moves after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, a US military official said, according to a Bloomberg report. The official described the strike on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) site as a response to Iranian aggression against US personnel and assets, the report said.

title: Kospi jumps over 3%; Asian markets rebound as Nvidia forecast lifts sentiment
